Title: Discovery and execution foundations
Summary: Structured discovery, standards, and agent/delivery rules were defined. The product began as a discovery-led orchestration system for HubSpot implementation work.

Title: Product reset and source-of-truth pack
Summary: The repo was reframed around a v1 operating model with product scope, architecture, domain model, roadmap, wireframes, and approval model. Docs became the main source of truth over the prototype.
Primary Docs: README.md; product-scope.md; architecture.md; domain-model.md; roadmap.md; mvp-wireframes.md; client-workspace-and-approval-model.md

Title: Sprint and execution expansion
Summary: Portal Ops, workers, task board, approvals, email tooling, UX redesign, and agent capability planning expanded the platform from concept into a more complete internal operating tool.
Primary Docs: platform-goal-alignment-report.md; sprint-portal-ops-execution-layer.md; sprint-01-job-worker.md; sprint-02-dashboard-agent-completion.md; sprint-03-cowork-perplexity-integration.md; sprint-04-task-board-approval-gates.md; sprint-05-security-data-model.md; sprint-06-email-composer-agenda-tool.md; sprint-07-ux-redesign.md

Title: Handoff and build-history layer
Summary: A large set of sprint and handoff docs captured implementation detail and short-term direction, but also created documentation clutter and made the active product narrative harder to scan.

Title: Retainers become first-class
Summary: Retainer logic moved into formal product territory, expanding the platform from project execution toward ongoing support, hour logic, and commercial operations.

Title: Magnisol exposes the next product shape
Summary: Real delivery pressure showed that discovery is often ongoing, workstreams matter, hours matter, and one connected project must support implementation, website, and client inputs together.

Title: Validation and local runbook
Summary: Acceptance walkthroughs, reconciliation checks, and local-dev guidance pushed the product closer to operational use rather than pure prototyping.

Title: Transnova-style optimisation and retainer workflow
Summary: The docs now explicitly recognise optimisation, retainer, client portal review, HubSpot connection, invoicing, and scoped follow-on work as real product needs. Discovery is no longer the only valid starting path.

Title: What the product is now
Summary: Muloo Deploy OS is now best understood as an internal delivery operating system for context capture, scoping, quoting, client collaboration, and delivery management across implementation, optimisation, and retained support.

Title: Clarify the main operating model
Summary: The next product step is to tighten coherence: make the front doors clearer, reduce discovery-first friction in optimisation flows, centralise Prepare/context, and archive historical sprint docs out of the active docs layer.
